reflections.summary: Game 3 and the 1-2 series loss came primarily from the Charizard-Y/Venusaur lead failing to convert its favorable Turn 1: Sleep Powder bought one inactive turn, but Charizard was then exposed to Sneasler's revealed Rock Slide and was KOed immediately. That removed sun, left Venusaur slow and vulnerable, and Mega Venusaur then cleanly controlled Tauros with Giga Drain while threatening Kingambit with Earth Power. The Tauros/Kingambit endgame also did not match their Mega Venusaur + Focus Sash Weavile structure: Tauros traded for Sneasler but was immediately KOed, and Kingambit could not finish Mega Venusaur before Weavile and Earth Power removed it. There were no recorded decision errors, so this was chiefly a matchup/preview and positioning problem rather than a piloting mistake. The adjustment from the prior games appears to have backfired insofar as Mega Charizard Y was brought and evolved into an opponent carrying both Rock Slide Sneasler and Mega Venusaur; sun did not provide a durable advantage once Charizard fell. Preparation did identify useful tools in Kingambit, Tauros, and Venusaur, but the selected four lacked a stable answer to opposing Mega Venusaur and had no safe contingency after Charizard's removal. Raichu was registered but not brought, and no evidence shows it would have solved Mega Venusaur; the omitted Sableye, Altaria, Emolga, and Avalugg cannot be claimed as better answers from this evidence.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, do not default to Mega Charizard Y into the Sneasler + Mega Venusaur core unless Charizard can be kept safe from Rock Slide and its sun turns produce immediate decisive value. Build preview around reliably pressuring Mega Venusaur first: retain Kingambit for it, avoid exposing Tauros to Giga Drain before Mega Venusaur is weakened, and account for Earth Power when choosing Kingambit's timing. Bring a four that can handle both Sneasler and Focus Sash Weavile without requiring Tauros to trade itself; prioritize immediate Steel pressure into Mega Venusaur/Weavile and a safer lead than Charizard-Y/Venusaur if Sneasler is likely. In preparation, reconsider the Venusaur and Charizard-Y mega plan for this matchup and test whether a registered alternative or a revised set offers more direct, durable Mega Venusaur counterplay; there is insufficient evidence that any left-behind Pokémon specifically would have fixed it.
reflections.notebook: Opponent durable facts: Jolly Life Orb Poison Touch Sneasler has Close Combat, Rock Slide, Gunk Shot, Protect; Rock Slide is a major deterrent to Mega Charizard Y. Modest Mega Venusaur has Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, Earth Power, Protect; it answers Aqua Tauros with Giga Drain and threatens Kingambit with Earth Power. Jolly Focus Sash Pressure Weavile has Icicle Crash, Ice Shard, Knock Off, Protect; assume Sash prevents a simple one-hit answer. Their remaining fourth was one of Skarmory, Incineroar, or Gardevoir, so do not treat any one as confirmed. Prep conclusion: opposing Mega Venusaur is the key structural problem; preserve and position Kingambit to pressure it, do not sacrifice Tauros into it, and avoid making Charizard-Y the central plan when Sneasler's Rock Slide is available.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series because the between-game adjustment to bring Venusaur-Mega and Sneasler broke the opponent's Charizard-Y sun core. Sneasler woke from Sleep Powder and Rock Slide OHKO'd Charizard, then Venusaur-Mega's Earth Power removed opposing Venusaur and later Kingambit. Weavile's Knock Off and Venusaur-Mega's Earth Power closed out after Sneasler traded for Tauros. Avoiding Incineroar entirely prevented Kingambit Defiant boosts, and the opponent's Kingambit Protect stall only delayed the inevitable Earth Power. The series was won 2-1 by leaning on Thick Fat Venusaur-Mega and Sneasler's coverage.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, I would keep Venusaur-Mega and Sneasler as the core but replace Incineroar with Farigiraf (Armor Tail) to block Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Raichu's Fake Out, giving a safer pivot that doesn't trigger Defiant. If Dragonite becomes a bigger threat, Skarmory is a better sixth than Incineroar. I would also consider Lum Berry on Sneasler over Life Orb to neutralize Sleep Powder, though Life Orb's extra power was valuable.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Charizard-Mega-Y often leads with Protect to bait attacks; Venusaur uses Sleep Powder early, often targeting Sneasler; Kingambit carries Chople Berry, Defiant, and tends to Protect when threatened before using Sucker Punch; Tauros-Paldea-Aqua has Intimidate and Wave Crash with recoil; Raichu and Dragonite were held back but remain threats. Strategic facts: Venusaur-Mega Thick Fat resists sun-boosted Fire and Earth Power hits Kingambit super effectively; Sneasler Rock Slide is the Charizard answer and Close Combat still chunks Kingambit through Chople; Weavile's Knock Off is useful but resisted by Kingambit; never bring Incineroar in while Kingambit is alive because Intimidate triggers Defiant. Prep conclusion: Venusaur-Mega + Sneasler + Weavile is the right core; Incineroar is a liability in this matchup and should be replaced with a priority blocker or a Dragonite check.
